item.title: What the situation in Venezuela means for Caribbean cruises
item.description: Several thousand passengers were affected by airspace restrictions over the weekend (3-4 January). While the situation has since stabilised, cruisers with upcoming Caribbean bookings should monitor how circumstances evolve.

item.title: Oceania Cruises is becoming an adults-only line
item.description: The luxury line has announced it is transitioning to a kids-free cruise experience, with all new bookings restricted to guests aged 18 and over.

item.description: World of Cruising TV is back on the small screen with fresh faces, new ships and real-life cruise stories

item.title: 14 new cruise ships launching in 2026
item.description: From family-friendly options to ultra-luxury boutique ships, here are the 2026 debuts worth knowing about.

item.title: Unrest in Mexico: what it means for cruise passengers
item.description: Following the killing of a cartel leader in Mexico, unrest has disrupted travel and prompted some cruise lines to alter schedules.

item.title: What the Middle East conflict means for cruise passengers
item.description: Select cruises have been impacted since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran on 28 February, with itinerary changes and cancellations affecting passengers in the region.

item.title: Is the Middle East war affecting Nile River cruises?
item.description: Several cruise lines have cancelled Nile sailings, including Avalon Waterways and Tauck.

item.title: Last chance: World of Cruising TV Season 4 is nearly over
item.description: Season 4 of World of Cruising TV is winding down, and if you haven't caught up yet, now's the moment. Along with the episodes themselves, you’ll find exclusive deals and competitions on the table, but not for much longer.

item.title: The cruise line turning the heads of Love Is Blind stars
item.description: Benaiah and Nicole Grünewald-Bridi weren’t cruise people. Here’s how sailing the Adriatic with Celestyal Cruises changed that.
